tasks.title: Scaffold Next.js project
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/001-scaffold. Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + ESLint, src/ layout. Brand strings centralised in src/lib/constants.ts (SITE_NAME). .env.local.example added; .gitignore already covers .env*. Build and lint pass clean. Repo had no commits, so main was created from the existing docs as a base for task branches.

tasks.title: Build the landing page from scratch
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/002-landing-page (branched off task/001, since main has no scaffold yet). Header, hero, how-it-works, gap-check form, footer. Original palette (galvanise/paper/zinc-dust/millscale/slate-wash/verdigris) and type pairing (Bricolage Grotesque over IBM Plex Sans/Mono); signature detail is a tape-measure tick rule in SVG. Icons are lucide-react, no emoji. Copy grounded in business-model.md with TODO-VERIFY comments guarding the unverified consultant figures and the compliance categories. Form renders but is not wired — submitting shows an honest 'not connected yet' notice for task 003 to replace. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Set up Supabase lead capture
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/003-supabase-lead-capture. The outstanding manual step is complete: the human ran supabase/migrations/0001_leads.sql in the Supabase SQL editor and confirmed a real form submission landed as a row in the leads table, which closes the one gap that was left unproven. Everything else was already done and verified against the live project: server action with server-side validation, allow-list checks on both dropdowns, field-level and form-level errors, values echoed back on failure, pending state, and a real success panel replacing the old 'not wired up yet' placeholder. Verified in the browser: validation rejects whitespace-only and malformed input, the database failure path shows a generic message while the real error goes to the server log only, and the success panel renders.

tasks.title: SEO essentials
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/004-seo (branched off task/002). sitemap.ts and robots.ts via Next.js file conventions, both driven by SITE_URL. JSON-LD Organization schema on the homepage, limited to facts that hold today. Canonical URL plus Open Graph and Twitter metadata. Heading hierarchy and lang verified in the rendered DOM. Alt text audit: no raster images exist yet, and all decorative SVGs are aria-hidden. Page is fully static; trimmed unused IBM Plex weights, which cut roughly 50KB of fonts and one preload. No OG image yet — deferred until the name and domain are settled. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Deploy to Vercel
tasks.notes: Prep is done on branch task/005-vercel-deploy and the repo is deploy-ready, but the deploy itself needs a human: importing the repo requires signing in to a Vercel account and granting it GitHub access, which I cannot and should not do. No Vercel CLI, token, or session exists in this environment either. Everything not requiring that account is finished and verified: main builds and lints clean and is fully static; NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL was confirmed to drive robots.txt, sitemap.xml, the canonical link, the Open Graph tags and the JSON-LD url; and a build with the Supabase variables removed was confirmed to still succeed, which is the main deploy trap. Step-by-step instructions, the env var table, and the verification checklist are in DEPLOY.md. Custom domain deliberately not attempted, as instructed.

tasks.title: Navbar, smooth scroll, and footer rework
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. Nav is a flat row of About/FAQ/Contact that stays visible at every width — no hamburger. 'Free gap check' is gone from the nav as asked; it survives as a footer link. Link list lives in src/lib/nav.ts so the header, footer and sitemap share one source. Header and footer moved from page.tsx into the root layout so every page gets the same chrome. Smooth scroll is CSS scroll-behavior on html, wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion so it costs no JS and respects the OS setting. Footer now carries the wordmark, the ISN/Avetta disclaimer, a page list, contact details, a tick rule, and a copyright line with the build year.

tasks.title: About, FAQ and Contact pages
tasks.notes: Three new pages, copy grounded in business-model.md and honest about being early stage. No invented founding story, team bios, or generic SaaS FAQ filler. Must match the existing palette, type scale, and tick-rule motif. Per-page Metadata API entries and sitemap updates.

tasks.title: Typography consistency audit
tasks.notes: Audit every page, old and new, for a consistent type scale and correct font usage — display face for headings, Plex Sans for body, Plex Mono for the small uppercase labels. Catch any default/system font creeping in on the new pages. Runs after 007 so there is something to audit.

tasks.title: Tagline exploration
tasks.notes: Draft several original tagline options grounded in business-model.md — the trigger event, the urgency, the consultant-vs-template contrast. Present the options with reasoning in the log, pick a default, and keep it swappable via lib/constants.ts. Sequenced before 010 because the OG image renders the chosen line.

tasks.title: Dynamic OG image
tasks.notes: Generate the 1200x630 OG image with next/og so it tracks the brand constants instead of going stale as a static file. Build on the tape-measure tick motif rather than centring the wordmark on an empty field. Needs the display font available to Satori, which next/font does not expose.

tasks.title: Vercel Speed Insights
tasks.notes: Install @vercel/speed-insights and mount <SpeedInsights /> from @vercel/speed-insights/next in the root layout, per Vercel's setup instructions. No further configuration. Data only appears once the site is deployed, which is still task 005.

blocked_on.action_needed: Import the repo into Vercel, set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, then submit the live form once and confirm the row lands in Supabase. Full runbook in DEPLOY.md. Do not attach a custom domain yet.
blocked_on.why_a_human: Connecting the repo means signing in to a Vercel account and authorising its GitHub access. There is no Vercel CLI, API token, or existing session in this environment, and entering account credentials is not something I should do on your behalf.
blocked_on.branch_note: Tasks 001, 002, 004 and 003 are all merged into main and pushed, in that order. task/005-vercel-deploy adds DEPLOY.md and this status update on top of main.
